findings.title: Stale denial-cache entries take precedence over fresher positive permission data
findings.body: In Check, the permission denial cache is consulted before the positive permission cache, and denial entries are never invalidated when the permission cache is refreshed. Sequence: (1) Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) misses the perm cache, the DB requery denies, and a denial entry is cached (30s TTL). (2) The user is then granted read on dash1. (3) Any other Check for this user+action that falls through to the DB (e.g. for dash2) refreshes permCache via getUserPermissions with fresh data that now includes dash1. (4) A retry of Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) hits the stale denial entry at line 117 and returns denied, even though the server's own freshly cached permission set says allow. The denial check should run after the positive cache check (allow on cached hit, then denial cache, then DB fallback), or denial entries for the user+action should be dropped when permCache is rewritten. As written, users can be denied access to just-granted resources for up to the full 30s TTL even when the server already holds fresh permissions proving the grant — which partially defeats the stated purpose of this PR (immediately accessing newly granted/created resources).

findings.title: Denial-precedence test uses a non-allowing cache entry, so it doesn't prove what its comment claims
findings.body: In TestService_CacheCheck/"Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the perm cache is seeded with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. Because checkPermission tests the truthiness of scopeMap[scope], a false value does not grant access, so this test would pass even if the denial cache were checked after the permission cache, or if the permission cache were consulted and simply found nothing allowing. To actually pin down the precedence behavior (denial cache wins over an allowing perm cache entry), the cached value must be true — which would currently fail and exposes the stale-denial-overrides-fresh-allow problem in Check.

findings.title: permissionCacheUsage metric recorded as a miss on a permission-cache hit that didn't grant access
findings.body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cached permission set but checkPermission does not allow the request (triggering the intended DB requery fallback), execution reaches line 137 and increments permissionCacheUsage with label "false" (miss), even though the permission cache was hit. Before this change the metric was incremented inside getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions strictly according to cache hit/miss, so dashboards and alerts built on the hit ratio will now show a drop in hit rate that does not reflect actual cache effectiveness. The hit should be recorded before evaluating checkPermission, with a separate metric (or label) for the fallback-to-DB path.
